recent_posts.title: This Week in Rails: May 1, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Weekly Rails update covering several notable changes: new Rails apps now enable frozen string literals by default via a bootsnap config file with corresponding RuboCop settings; a bug fix for find_signed on models with composite primary keys; and a fix allowing aliases for unions in FROM clauses (previously broken in PostgreSQL). Community input is also requested on updated guides for Asset Pipeline, Layouts & Rendering, Caching, and Active Job Basics. Applications for the Rails at Scale Summit (Sept 22, Austin) close May 8.

recent_posts.title: Active Record gets better every week
recent_posts.summary: Weekly roundup of Ruby on Rails changes including bumping the minimum supported PostgreSQL version to 10.0, a fix to raise an error when null: true is passed for primary keys in add_column, a 2x performance improvement for merging ActiveRecord::Relation extensions, a fix for nested with_connection incorrectly clearing sticky lease flags, and a fix for Rails hanging when ffmpeg is spawned for video previews in ActiveStorage.

recent_posts.title: Great big Rails World 2026 update: CFP, Corporate Support tickets, workshops
recent_posts.summary: Rails World 2026 is heading to Austin, Texas on September 23-24, with capacity for 1,200 attendees. The CFP is now open until May 16 via Sessionize, covering themes like Rails 8 in production, AI-assisted development, and frontend focus. Workshops are planned for September 22, with hands-on 4-hour sessions. The Rails at Scale Summit returns as an invite-only event (capped at 150) on the day before, with applications due May 8. Corporate Support tickets are available now at $1,300, while General Admission tickets ($699) go on sale May 12 at 10am CT.

recent_posts.title: Query command for database queries and more
recent_posts.summary: This week in Rails covers several new features and fixes. The headline addition is the `rails query` command, a read-only database query tool that accepts ActiveRecord expressions and returns structured JSON output with metadata including SQL, row count, and query time. Subcommands like `query schema`, `query models`, and `query explain` are also included. Other changes include appending `charset=utf-8` to Content-Type headers for static CSS and HTML files, adding an offline fallback page to the PWA scaffold, a rewrite of the Layouts and Rendering guide, a performance improvement using hash lookup for exact-match regexp filters in ParameterFilter, and a clarification of Active Storage security around signed URLs.

recent_posts.title: Explicit query: and body: kwargs for integration tests and more!
recent_posts.summary: This week in Rails covers several notable changes: new explicit `query:` and `body:` kwargs for integration test helpers resolve ambiguity with GET+JSON requests in API-only apps; two new predicate methods `request.safe_method?` and `request.unsafe_method?` are added to ActionDispatch::Request per RFC 9110; Action Cable's origin check is updated to respect `X-Forwarded-Host` for correct behavior behind reverse proxies; and a rewrite of the Layouts and Rendering guide is open for community review.

recent_posts.title: Speedup ActiveRecord::LogSubscriber#sql_color and more!
recent_posts.summary: A weekly roundup of Rails codebase changes covering performance improvements, bug fixes, and deprecations. Highlights include anchoring regexp patterns in ActiveRecord::LogSubscriber#sql_color to avoid timeout issues, a fast path for string cache keys in ActiveSupport::Cache, predefined Postgres type OIDs to eliminate per-connection pg_type queries, deprecation of the MySQL strict option and PostgreSQL schema_order option, Unicode fix for Inflector#titleize, composite key fixes in associations, and the addition of an AGENTS.md guide for AI coding agents contributing to Rails.

recent_posts.title: This Week in Rails: March 27, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Weekly Rails changelog covering security releases (7.2.3.1, 8.0.4.1, 8.1.2.1) and bugfix releases (8.0.5, 8.1.3). Notable changes include: `validates` now combines top-level and per-validator `:if`/`:unless`/`:on` options instead of silently overriding; `titleize` now correctly capitalizes Unicode characters; and MySQL's ER_NO_DB_ERROR is now classified as `ActiveRecord::ConnectionFailed` for automatic retry.

recent_posts.title: Rails Versions 8.0.5 and 8.1.3 have been released!
recent_posts.summary: Ruby on Rails versions 8.0.5 and 8.1.3 have been released as regular bugfix updates. Both releases include fixes from the previous day's security releases (7.2.3.1, 8.0.4.1, and 8.1.2.1). Rails 8.1 will continue receiving bug fixes until October 2026, while Rails 8.0 transitions to security-only updates in May, making 8.0.5 potentially the last bugfix release in that series. SHA-256 checksums are provided for all gem packages.

recent_posts.title: Rails Versions 7.2.3.1, 8.0.4.1, and 8.1.2.1 have been released!
recent_posts.summary: Security patch releases for Ruby on Rails versions 7.2.3.1, 8.0.4.1, and 8.1.2.1 have been published, addressing 10 security vulnerabilities. Users are strongly encouraged to upgrade immediately. Older versions are unsupported, with 7.2 being the minimum recommended series. SHA-256 hashes are provided for gem verification.

recent_posts.title: This Week in Rails: March 20, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Weekly roundup of Rails codebase changes including: batching SQL statements during schema loading for performance, deprecation of require_dependency (to be removed in Rails 9), new MySQL lock and algorithm options for DDL operations enabling online schema changes, Dockerfile build optimizations for new Rails apps, PostgreSQL RESET support on readonly queries, and Action Text improvements allowing block children alongside value in editor elements.

top_posts.title: Ruby on Rails — The Rails Foundation kicks off with one million dollars
top_posts.summary: The Rails Foundation kicks off with one million dollars today. Its mission is to improve the documentation, education, marketing, and events in our ecosystem. It will work to ensure a prosperous ecosystem that continues to improve, and becomes even more attractive to newcomers going forward.

top_posts.title: Ruby on Rails — Rails World 2025: Save the date
top_posts.summary: Rails World 2025 will take place on September 4 and 5, 2025, in Amsterdam. More tickets will be available this year. The CFP will open in early spring 2025, and tickets will be released shortly after. Sponsorship details will be available soon. The event will be held in the same venue as previous years to optimize logistics and focus on program and content.

top_posts.title: Ruby on Rails — Kamal 2, Bye-bye Sprockets, and so much more!
top_posts.summary: This post covers the latest changes in the Ruby on Rails codebase, including updates for Ruby on Rails Kamal 2, the removal of the Sucker Punch Active Job adapter, and the ability to use multiple rate limits per controller. It also highlights improvements such as the inclusion of options in cache delete events, new settings for ActiveRecord attributes inspection, support for dropping multiple tables at once, and the introduction of the Parameters#expect method for safer parameter handling.

top_posts.title: Ruby on Rails — New database sharding methods, improved Active Record Migration Docs, caching improvements for ActiveStorage and more!
top_posts.summary: Recent updates to Ruby on Rails include improved Active Record Migration documentation, new methods for database sharding in ActiveRecord::Base, enhanced caching for ActiveStorage, deferred generation of assertion failure messages in Minitest, and rubocop-compliant code generation with 'g scaffold' when no fields are specified. Fixes also include properly ignoring parent class methods in alias_attribute.

top_posts.summary: The Rails World 2024 speaker list is live, featuring speakers who will discuss new tools, enhancing Rails, database performance, Rails upgrades, accessibility, and security.
